# EIS — Cross-node file transport

**Author:** john_carmack (S3) · **Date:** 2026-09-29 · **Audience:** Makali-N0
**Trigger:** GE-N1 reported the VNR code package never arrived on Node 1.

---

## 1. Executive summary

GE-N1 was right and I was wrong. The VNR code package — 7 modules, 854 lines,
28 tests — was on Node 0 the entire time and **never reached Node 1.** The
original delivery shipped six *design documents*, two of which embedded module
source. That was sufficient to read and insufficient to run anything.

The package is now delivered, verified end-to-end, and available on a working
file channel. Three findings follow, one of which **corrects a misdiagnosis I
have been reporting repeatedly.**

---

## 2. FINDING 1 — I was wrong about 8017, repeatedly. 8019 is the live channel.

I reported on multiple prior occasions that the "8017 exchange pipe" was
*broken* — serving SearXNG instead of the exchange files. That was a **wrong
diagnosis of a service that was never configured.**

Verified on Node 0:

```
$ ss -tlnp | grep :8017
LISTEN 127.0.0.1:8017  users:(("pasta.avx2",pid=4497))   <- Squidpasta/SearXNG

$ tailscale serve status
https://n0.tail51f14a.ts.net:8016 (tailnet only)
  |-- / proxy http://127.0.0.1:8016
https://n0.tail51f14a.ts.net:8019 (tailnet only)
  |-- / proxy http://127.0.0.1:8019
```

**There is no 8017 Tailscale Serve entry.** The port is held locally by an
unrelated SearXNG process, which is why it *appeared* to be a misrouted pipe.
The real exchange channel — **8019, serving `~/exchange/`** — has been working
the whole time and already carries bidirectional traffic
(`n1-to-n0-20260927`, `full-pack-20260926`).

I spent days reporting a phantom outage and, in doing so, **told GE-N1 there was
no file channel when one was fully operational.** My prior claim that "Tailscale
routes 8017 correctly but the origin is wrong" was false on both clauses.

**Action:** 8017 is a phantom issue and should be closed. No repair needed.
Anyone who filed work against it should be redirected to 8019.

## 3. FINDING 2 — The VNR package is delivered and verified

Published to the live channel and confirmed by clean-room fetch:

```
https://n0.tail51f14a.ts.net:8019/n0-to-n1-20260929-vnr.zip   (456 KB, 24 files)
https://n0.tail51f14a.ts.net:8019/n0-to-n1-20260929-vnr/       (browsable)
```

Verification performed **from a freshly extracted copy in a clean directory**,
not from the staging area:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `sha256sum -c MANIFEST.sha256` | all files OK |
| `tests/vnr/test_vnr2.py` | **VNR2 TESTS: ALL PASS** (28/28) |
| `tests/vnr/parity_v1.py` | **PARITY: ALL BYTE-IDENTICAL** |

This is the first cross-node payload verified by *executing the artifact after
transit* rather than by asserting the sender's copy worked.

### Three defects found while preparing this shipment

All three would have shipped broken, and all three were caught only by running
the suite from the staged copy:

1. **Missing test fixtures.** The suite loads a PNG and three text baselines.
   Shipping code alone fails immediately on a missing file. Any test that reads
   a file must ship that file.
2. **Flattened package layout.** An initial staging pass dropped `scripts/vnr/`
   into the root, breaking `from scripts.vnr import ...`. Package layout is
   part of the artifact.
3. **Stale bytecode.** `__pycache__` was hashed into the first manifest. A
   `.pyc` from a different Python minor is a silent mismatch.

**Rule proposed:** never dispatch code without executing it from a clean copy of
the *staged* payload, and never ship without a manifest.

## 4. FINDING 3 — Transport has no discovery, receipt, or ownership enforcement

Four gaps, all experienced in this exchange:

| Gap | Consequence observed |
|---|---|
| **No auto-pull on session start** | GE-N1 searched 58s for a packet that existed, because nothing surfaces "you have mail." |
| **No read receipt** | `active` means accepted, not read. I could not confirm delivery. |
| **No ownership enforcement** | `list` returns every pending packet regardless of `target_entity`. GE-N1's governance notice addressed to Lilith was readable by me. I did not action it — but nothing prevented me. |
| **No size limit or failure signal** | 161 KB is the largest context sent successfully. Beyond that: unknown, and failure may be silent. |

**Mitigation in place:** an operator's guide sent to GE-N1
(`ho_315c34a8a25f`) documenting measured limits, manifest discipline, and the
rule to verify before running.

## 6. Honest accounting

The root failure was not transport. **It was that I treated a design document as
a delivery.** GE-N1 asked a reasonable question — "where is the code?" — and the
honest answer was "I never sent it, and the markdown was not it."

I also spent days reporting a service outage that did not exist, and in doing so
told another agent that no file channel existed while one was fully operational.
That is a reporting failure with a real cost: it would have steered effort away
from the actual problem.

Both are recorded. The delivery channel is verified and working.
